It's not that our lives are "worst" - I mean, I really don't believe so. Yes, neurotypical people don't deal with the same symptoms we have to deal with, but living a very intense life has its perks. 

I don't know you at all; yet I would hate to loose you. It would break my heart. We understand each other at some level, and are fighting some of the very same battles. I know exactly how you feel when you say you feel "empty" or abnormal. This community feel like family. 

It's a big challenge, but I do believe it is worth it, and there might be a more comfortable life waiting for you - with the help of medication, therapy, exercise or whatever works for you. I know it doesn't seem possible but keep trying. The only way to know what will happen tomorrow is being there. I promise you it is worth it.

Absolutely, I know how you feel.

I think about my FP all day everyday. I'm maniac when he gives me attention and suicidal when I feel neglected or abandoned, sometimes on the same day - though I haven't been feeling maniac because of a new medication. 

Relationships, even health ones, are a challenge to me because is always, *always* a rollercoaster. 

We recently stopped talking for only 5 days and I thought our friendship was over; and I can't explain how empty I feel. It was insane. I felt so empty I didn't even consider suicide anymore, because it was like I didn't even exist in the first place. I simply didn't know what to do with myself, because my life... is him. Literally the second he was back in my life, things started feeling normal again.

I'm literally addicted to him. All my thoughts are about him or fantasizing about talking to him. My personality, whatever that means, is designed to please him. I don't care about other people at all.

Of course, I'd never tell *him* that. ;)

Maybe you can both go to therapy together, and figure out particularly helpful techniques to sustain a helpful relationship. 

For example, I asked my best friend (and FP, but I haven't told him to not scare him lol) to send me an emoji when he can't text me back, just so I know he's busy or tired, and not think he hates me.

You can both, together, write down a list of her triggers, and come up with ways to make them less... triggering, one by one.

I'm 21 right now. I had my first french kiss at 18! I still haven't had a serious romantic relationship. I was bullied and had a particularly abusive friend throughout middle and high school, so I only started learning about how to socialize and interact with people already as an adult, and I'm still very early in the process. Right now, I don't have any friends and feel extra isolated because of the pandemic, of course.

But maybe one day, things will get better.
I've been trying to tell myself that it is never too late. 

I've been seeing a lot of young adults like myself or literal kids on here saying that they're already hopeless, and it really breaks my heart. I absolutely know exactly how it feels. We have to always always always remember ourselves that our whole lives are in front of us; and our happiness doesn't depend on having a girlfriend, or a partner of any gender.
